explanation: Singapore isn't especially strict about affection in public compared to its neighbors, but overt displays like prolonged kissing or groping are generally seen as inappropriate and can draw disapproving looks, particularly from older generations. Brief hand-holding or a quick hug is unlikely to bother anyone; there's no law against ordinary PDA between consenting adults, unlike some neighboring countries.
local_tip: Casual hand-holding or a quick hug is fine almost anywhere; save more intimate affection for private settings, especially around family-oriented or religious spaces.
regional_note: Older and more religiously conservative Singaporeans (including many Malay-Muslim and Indian families) tend to view public affection less favorably than younger, more Westernized Singaporeans.

also_check.note: PDA is uncommon and can draw attention; even hand-holding is often reserved for younger couples.
Kissing and casual affection in public are common and not considered inappropriate.
Public affection beyond hand-holding between unmarried couples can be illegal and lead to fines or detention.
